findings.evidence: `Limits.lean:62` introduces `(Matrix.of L).PosSemidef` only to strip it at 87-90; `Gaussian/Basic.lean:121-131` closes the same `charFun_posSemidef … |>.submatrix` step with `rw [heq]; exact hscaled`, no peel, versus `Convention.lean:119-138` which spends 20 lines on `heq ▸` then `hof ▸`.
findings.fix: In `Limits.lean` state `have hOf : Matrix.PosSemidef L` directly and drop `hof`. Remove the leftover `Matrix.of` from the statements that force the other two peels — the private `posSemidef_of_support_posSemidef` (Kernel/Basic.lean:56-59) and `TauCeti.charFun_posSemidef` (Bochner/CharFun/PosDef.lean:124) — so they match the wrapper-free convention this PR adopts elsewhere.
findings.issue: Three copies of an undocumented `Matrix.of f = f` peel proved by `ext; rfl` (`Limits.lean:87-89`, `Fourier/Convention.lean:134-137`, `CharFun/PositiveDefinite.lean:59-62`). `Matrix.of` is `Equiv.refl` (mathlib/Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/Matrix/Defs.lean:88), so these transports are defeq no-ops that Mathlib deliberately keeps explicit to avoid Pi-vs-Matrix instance confusion; nothing documents why the crossing is safe.

findings.evidence: `Matrix.hadamard_apply` exists at mathlib/Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/Matrix/Hadamard.lean:49; `SemigroupGroup/Basic.lean:352` is `hF.posSemidef.smul (α := ℝ) hr` with no transport while 341-345 builds one for `k • K`.
findings.fix: Prove these with the named lemmas (`Matrix.hadamard_apply`, `Pi.add_apply`, `Pi.smul_apply`) instead of `rfl`, and use one idiom consistently for `add`/`const_mul`/`mul`/`smul_of_nonneg` rather than alternating between a silent `exact` and a 5-line `heq ▸` bridge.
findings.issue: Equalities between a matrix operation and its pointwise lambda are proved by unfolding the operation definitionally with `ext; rfl`, with no comment: `Closure.lean:82-86` (`Matrix.hadamard`), `SemigroupGroup/Basic.lean:327-332` (`Pi` add), `SemigroupGroup/Basic.lean:360-365` (`Matrix.hadamard`). Meanwhile `SemigroupGroup/Basic.lean:349-352` crosses the same class of defeq silently with `exact`, so adjacent lemmas use opposite conventions.

findings.evidence: Compare `Kernel/Closure.lean:60` (`rwa [heq] at h`) and `:72` (`exact heq ▸ h`) with `:100`'s `congrArg` form for the same transport.
findings.fix: Replace both with `rwa [heq] at hpd` / `rwa [heq] at h`.
findings.issue: `exact (congrArg (fun K => Matrix.PosSemidef K) heq).mp hpd` (also `Kernel/Closure.lean:100`) is an obfuscated spelling of a rewrite; the same PR uses `heq ▸ h` or `rwa [heq] at h` for the identical step in a dozen other places.

summary: The migration replaces the deleted kernel wrappers with hand-rolled equality transports, several of which are pure `Matrix.of` defeq no-ops, and the same step is spelled three different ways across the PR (silent `exact`, `rw [heq]`, and a 20-line `heq ▸`/`hof ▸` chain). Fix the wrapper mismatch at its source and settle on one idiom.
